## Overview

Once a research lab has verified offline network isolation and scrubbed direct
identifiers under HIPAA Safe Harbor, three practical questions remain before
running production extractions and sharing derived tables with collaborators:

1. **How reliable are local 7B–14B open-weights extractions across seeds and
   prompt phrasings?** Use `airgap_extract_consensus()` to execute crossed
   multi-pass self-consistency runs and inspect per-row agreement and
   long-format pass reliability data.
2. **Could indirect quasi-identifiers (`site`, `age_band`, `wave`, `zip3`)
   re-identify individuals in an exported analytic table?** Audit tables with
   `assess_reidentification_risk()` and enforce $k$-anonymity and
   $l$-diversity with `apply_k_anonymity()`.
3. **Which quantization, context window, and batch size best fit our lab GPU
   or HPC allocation—and how long will 10,000 rows take?** Size hardware with
   `recommend_runtime_config()` and measure real pilot throughput with
   `benchmark_local_runtime()`.

```{r load}
library(airgapllm)
library(tibble)
data("synthetic_notes", package = "airgapllm")
```

## 1. Multi-Pass Self-Consistency & Consensus Extraction

Local quantized models can exhibit occasional stochastic or prompt-framing
sensitivity on borderline clinical notes. `airgap_extract_consensus()` runs a
deterministic grid of random `seeds` and/or `prompt_templates` over the
already-sanitized corpus, aggregating categorical/logical fields by majority
vote and numeric/integer fields by median or trimmed mean:

```{r consensus}
clinical_schema <- extraction_schema(
  sentiment = schema_field("enum", values = c("positive", "neutral", "negative")),
  severity = schema_field("integer", min = 0L, max = 10L),
  crisis_flag = schema_field("logical"),
  name = "consensus_coding_v1"
)

prompts <- c(
  concise = "Classify sentiment, severity (0-10), and crisis_flag from this record:\n{text}",
  clinical = "As a clinical rater, return strict JSON coding for this note:\n{text}"
)

work_dir <- tempfile("airgap_v04_")
dir.create(work_dir)
audit_file <- file.path(work_dir, "consensus_audit.jsonl")

# 2 prompts x 2 seeds = 4 crossed passes per document
cons_res <- airgap_extract_consensus(
  data = synthetic_notes[1:6, ],
  text_col = "note_text",
  schema = clinical_schema,
  runtime = runtime_mock(model = "llama3.1:8b-instruct-q4_K_M", seed = 100L),
  seeds = c(100L, 200L),
  prompt_templates = prompts,
  id_col = "note_id",
  numeric_agg = "median",
  tie_policy = "first",
  audit_log_path = audit_file
)

cons_res
```

Inspect field-level consensus diagnostics and the long-format pass table
(`unit_id`, `pass_id`, `prompt_id`, `seed`, plus all typed schema columns),
which is directly structured for multi-facet psychometric reliability modeling
(such as Generalizability Theory / G-studies; when loading alongside other LLM
evaluation packages that also export `schema_field()`, qualify calls as
`airgapllm::schema_field()`):

```{r consensus-diag}
consensus_diagnostics(cons_res)
head(consensus_passes(cons_res), 8L)
audit_log_verify(audit_file)
```

## 2. Quasi-Identifier $k$-Anonymity & $l$-Diversity Export Audits

Removing direct identifiers (names, emails, SSNs, MRNs) does **not** guarantee
anonymity if combinations of indirect quasi-identifiers (such as study `site`,
`age_band`, and `wave`) single out small subgroups.

Consider a synthetic extracted clinical table prepared for secondary analysis:

```{r reid-risk}
export_df <- tibble(
  site = c(rep("Site_North", 6), rep("Site_South", 2), "Site_East", rep("Site_West", 5)),
  age_band = c(rep("30-39", 6), rep("50-59", 2), "70-79", rep("30-39", 5)),
  severity_tier = c(
    "mild", "moderate", "mild", "mild", "severe", "moderate",
    "severe", "severe",
    "severe",
    "mild", "moderate", "severe", "mild", "moderate"
  )
)

# Audit against k >= 5 anonymity and l >= 2 distinct severity outcomes per class
risk_before <- assess_reidentification_risk(
  data = export_df,
  quasi_ids = c("site", "age_band"),
  k_min = 5L,
  sensitive_col = "severity_tier",
  l_min = 2L
)
risk_before
```

Notice that `Site_South` ($k = 2$, $l = 1$) and `Site_East` ($k = 1$, a sample
unique with prosecutor risk $1.00$) fail both $k$-anonymity and $l$-diversity.
Compare the two safe mitigation strategies in `apply_k_anonymity()`:

```{r apply-k}
# Option A: Suppress violating rows cleanly
suppressed <- apply_k_anonymity(
  data = export_df,
  quasi_ids = c("site", "age_band"),
  k_min = 5L,
  strategy = "suppress_rows",
  sensitive_col = "severity_tier",
  l_min = 2L
)
suppressed

# Option B: Mask rare classes (progressively absorbing smallest residual class so
# the masked fallback class itself strictly satisfies k >= 5 and l >= 2)
masked <- apply_k_anonymity(
  data = export_df,
  quasi_ids = c("site", "age_band"),
  k_min = 5L,
  strategy = "mask_rare",
  sensitive_col = "severity_tier",
  l_min = 2L
)
masked
```

Both strategies reduce maximum prosecutor risk from `1.0000` to `<= 0.2000` and
achieve `PASS` on both $k$-anonymity and $l$-diversity without logging any raw
participant values.

## 3. Hardware-Aware Auto-Tuning & Throughput Benchmarking

Before launching a 10,000-row extraction job on a lab workstation or university
HPC GPU node, query `recommend_runtime_config()` to select an OOM-safe
parameter tier, quantization, context window, batch size, and container memory
limits:

```{r auto-tuner}
# Single 24 GB lab workstation GPU (e.g., RTX 4090 / L4)
rec_ws <- recommend_runtime_config(
  vram_gb = 24,
  ram_gb = 64,
  n_gpus = 1L,
  n_docs = 10000L,
  avg_tokens = 1100L,
  priority = "balanced",
  backend = "ollama"
)
rec_ws

# Multi-GPU HPC node (2x 80 GB A100/H100) tuned for accuracy on vLLM
rec_hpc <- recommend_runtime_config(
  vram_gb = 80,
  ram_gb = 256,
  n_gpus = 2L,
  n_docs = 25000L,
  avg_tokens = 1500L,
  priority = "accuracy",
  backend = "vllm"
)
rec_hpc
```

Finally, run a quick pilot benchmark via `benchmark_local_runtime()` to measure
empirical throughput, p50/p95 per-row latency, repair retry rate, and projected
walltime ETA for your full corpus:

```{r benchmark}
bm <- benchmark_local_runtime(
  runtime = runtime_mock(
    model = "llama3.1:8b-instruct-q4_K_M",
    seed = 42L,
    malform_schedule = list(BM_0002 = c("{invalid_json"))
  ),
  schema = clinical_schema,
  data = synthetic_notes,
  text_col = "note_text",
  n_sample = 8L,
  corpus_size = 10000L
)
bm
```

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(work_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
